todaysEvents.delta: AP reported renewed US-Iran strikes on Sep 1; the Iran-Oman traffic-management plan remains conditional and no signed commercial reopening has been verified.
AP reported UKMTO reports of two tanker incidents in and around Hormuz on Sep 1; no casualties were immediately reported, but route clearance remains unverified.
LNG Industry reported Edison received a further QatarEnergy force-majeure notice for five additional cargoes; the reported total is 29 cargoes and the period extends into early November.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs into early November.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A failed framework, renewed tanker attacks or sanctions retaliation could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.

Working range $75-85 base (signed workable deal); $85-105 stress (conditional routing); $105-135+ tail (renewed closure).
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $22.00/MMBtu (Jul 24, Reuters September-delivery assessment) as sustained Hormuz disruption tightened Asian LNG balances; carried at $22.00 pending a newer weekly assessment. Contextual CFD reference $23.62/MMBtu (Trading Economics, Sep 1), up 4.01%. QatarEnergy force majeure now extends into early November after a further five-cargo notice reported by LNG Industry; 21 of 29 affected cargoes were reported replaced as of Aug 28.
